# rbe

rbe is an implementation of the RuleFit model of [Friedman and Popescu
(2008)](https://doi.org/10.1214/07-AOAS148) that uses modern boosting
methods such as XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost.

The model has two parts:

- A boosted tree that generates a set of rules, which are logical
  statements that describe the variables used to get to the terminal
  nodes of the tree.
- A regularized generalized linear model that takes the original
  predictors as well as a large set of binary indicators generated from
  the rule set.

## Installation

You can install the released version of rbe from
[CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org) with:

``` r

install.packages("rbe")
```

You can install the development version of rbe from
[GitHub](https://github.com/tidymodels/rbe) with:

``` r

pak::pak("tidymodels/rbe")
```

The xgboost and lightgbm packages are on CRAN. The catboost package is
not on CRAN; see the [catboost installation
instructions](https://catboost.ai/docs/en/installation/r-installation-binary-installation)
to install it.

## Example

This example fits a RuleFit model to predict delivery times. The rules
are made with xgboost:

``` r

library(rbe)
```

``` r

set.seed(273)
in_train <- 
  modeldata::deliveries |> 
  nrow() |> 
  sample.int(8000)

delivery_train <- modeldata::deliveries[in_train, ]
delivery_test <- modeldata::deliveries[-in_train, ]
```

``` r

set.seed(871)
rf_fit <- rule_ensemble(time_to_delivery ~ ., data = delivery_train, method = "xgboost")
rf_fit
#> RuleFit Using XGBoost
#> 
#> Training Set:
#> ℹ Samples: 8000
#> 
#> ℹ Predictors: 30
#> 
#> ℹ Rules: 222
#> 
#> 
#> Arguments:
#> • trees: 50
#> 
#> • mtry: 1
#> 
#> • learn_rate: 0.01
#> 
#> • tree_depth: 4
#> 
#> • min_n: 5
#> 
#> • penalty: 0.001
#> 
#> • mixture: 1
#> 
#> • verbose: FALSE
#> 
#> • counts: FALSE

rf_pred <- 
  predict(rf_fit, new_data = delivery_test) |> 
  dplyr::bind_cols(delivery_test)
```

``` r

library(ggplot2)

rf_pred |> 
  ggplot(aes(.pred, time_to_delivery)) + 
  geom_abline(col = "green") + 
  geom_point(alpha = 2 / 3) +
  theme_bw()
```

![Observed versus predicted delivery times for the test
set.](reference/figures/README-pred-plot-1.png)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`autoplot(`*`<rule_ensemble>`*`)`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/autoplot.rule_ensemble.md)
  : Create a ggplot for a glmnet object
- [`boosting_method()`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/boosting_method.md)
  [`values_boosting_method`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/boosting_method.md)
  : Parameter for the boosting method
- [`model_matrix_sep()`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/model_matrix_sep.md)
  : Create a model matrix with separated indicator column names
- [`multi_predict(`*`<rule_ensemble>`*`)`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/multi_predict.rule_ensemble.md)
  [`has_multi_predict(`*`<rule_ensemble>`*`)`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/multi_predict.rule_ensemble.md)
  [`multi_predict_args(`*`<rule_ensemble>`*`)`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/multi_predict.rule_ensemble.md)
  : Model predictions across many sub-models
- [`rule_ensemble-object`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/rule_ensemble-object.md)
  [`rule_ensemble_object`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/rule_ensemble-object.md)
  : RuleFit Model Objects
- [`rule_ensemble()`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/rule_ensemble.md)
  : Fit a RuleFit Model
- [`show_rule()`](https://tidymodels.github.io/rbe/reference/show_rule.md)
  : Show a Specific Rule
